title: Technical Data Packages
summary: Defines DoD requirements for the content, format, and structure of a Technical Data Package (TDP) — the authoritative technical description of an item, used to support acquisition, production, inspection, engineering, and logistics support.

title: TDP Levels — Conceptual, Developmental, Product
summary: TDPs progress through three levels: Conceptual (design concepts, sketches/renderings for analysis), Developmental (sufficient data for prototype fabrication or limited production), and Product (full design/manufacturing/inspection/QA data needed for a competent manufacturer to duplicate the item without further design engineering).

title: TDP Types — 2D and 3D
summary: TDP type describes the form/format of the technical data: Type 2D is based on 2-dimensional engineering drawings (ASME Y14.100 series); Type 3D is based on product model data and may include 3D native models, 2D drawings derived from them, 3Di PDF viewables, and neutral files.

title: TDP Elements
summary: TDP elements are the components that make up a Technical Data Package: engineering design data, Special Inspection Equipment (SIE) data, specifications, software documentation, Special Packaging Instruction (SPI) data, quality assurance provisions (QAP), and special tooling data.

title: TDP Data Management Products
summary: Data management products used by the procuring activity to control and manage TDP development: the Technical Data Package List (TDPL), document number assignment report, critical manufacturing process description, source control approval request, and engineering drawing tree.

title: Defense and Program-Unique Specifications Format and Content
summary: MIL-STD-961E (w/Change 4) establishes format and content requirements for defense specifications (used across multiple programs, coordinated and indexed in the ASSIST database) and program-unique specifications (developed for a single program/system), plus specification sheets, supplements, revisions, amendments, and notices. Every specification follows the same six-section format: Scope, Applicable Documents, Requirements, Verification, Packaging, and Notes. This standard integrated program-unique specification requirements previously covered by MIL-STD-490, Specification Practices, which it canceled.

title: Six-Section Specification Format
summary: The standard specification structure used throughout DoD acquisition documents: Section 1 Scope (brief abstract, no requirements), Section 2 Applicable Documents, Section 3 Requirements (what the entity must meet), Section 4 Verification (how compliance is confirmed), Section 5 Packaging, and Section 6 Notes (not contractually binding — general/explanatory information only, e.g. intended use, tailoring guidance).

title: Specification Types
summary: Defense specifications are either performance specifications (states required results and verification criteria, not the method) or detail specifications (specifies design requirements — materials, how to build it); a general specification covers requirements common to a group of parts and is paired with specification sheets for style/type/class/grade variants. Program-unique specifications further divide into item, material, process, software, and system specifications, based on what they describe (parts/components, raw/processed materials, fabrication procedures, software requirements, or a whole system).

title: Specification Identifiers — MIL-PRF / MIL-DTL
summary: A coordinated defense specification identifier is 'MIL-' plus 'PRF' (performance) or 'DTL' (detail) plus an Arabic numeral, e.g. MIL-PRF-123 or MIL-DTL-123. A limited-coordination specification (covering items needed by only one activity/Department/Agency) adds a parenthetical SD-1 symbol suffix, e.g. MIL-PRF-12345(CR). An interim (not-yet-fully-coordinated) specification is prefixed with '00', e.g. MIL-PRF-00915(SH), with the '00' and suffix removed once fully approved. A 'SUPERSEDING' block on the first page names the document(s) it replaces.

title: Specification Practices
summary: Canceled. MIL-STD-490's specification practices were integrated into and replaced by MIL-STD-961 (Defense and Program-Unique Specifications Format and Content); do not use MIL-STD-490 for new specifications. Referenced only historically by DOD-STD-2101(OS) — for items described by specifications prepared under the (now-canceled) MIL-STD-490, classification codes were annotated in Section 3 (Requirements) and Section 5 (Packaging/Preparation for Delivery).
cited_in: DOD-STD-2101(OS) §2.1 / §5.2; canceled and absorbed by MIL-STD-961

title: Data Item Descriptions (DIDs)
summary: MIL-STD-963C establishes format and content requirements for Data Item Descriptions (DIDs) — the standardization documents that define the data content, format, and intended use required of a contractor, paired with the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL, DD Form 1423) that identifies which DIDs apply to a contract. A DID may be self-contained (a complete description with no external references) or abstract-reference (describing data by pointing to other documents). DIDs must not direct work tasks (e.g. inspection, testing, 'the contractor shall...') — those belong in the contract statement of work; a DID only specifies the data product's content and format.

title: DID Structure — Self-Contained vs. Abstract-Reference
summary: Two authorized DID structures: a self-contained DID is a complete description of data content, format, and intended use with no reference to other documents (preferred, since it minimizes referenced documents); an abstract-reference DID instead points to other documents for additional content/format/intended-use information, used when that information is too voluminous to include directly.

title: Standard Practice for Military Packaging
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B as the standard practice governing military packaging requirements, relevant to Special Packaging Instruction (SPI) TDP elements.

title: Classification of Characteristics
summary: DOD-STD-2101(OS) establishes requirements and procedures for classifying the essential design characteristics of an item — appearing in its drawings and specifications — as Critical, Major, or Minor, based on the CLIFS criteria (Coordination, Life, Interchangeability, Function, Safety). Classification is performed by the design activity prior to release of the associated drawings/specifications, informing government inspection sampling, waiver/deviation approval authority, and inspection effort allocation.

title: CLIFS Classification Criteria
summary: The five criteria (Coordination, Life, Interchangeability, Function, Safety — acronym CLIFS) used to determine a characteristic's classification: Coordination (features affected by mating/assembly/integration with adjoining items), Life (service/storage/fatigue life, durability, reliability, environmental resistance), Interchangeability (form/fit/function enabling common use or replacement), Function (ability to perform intended purpose), and Safety (risk to personnel from the item's integrity or proper functioning).

title: Classification Codes — Critical, Major, Minor
summary: Characteristics are annotated on drawings/specifications with a category code letter: Critical = 'C' (likely, if defective, to create/increase a safety hazard or cause failure of a weapon system/major system to perform its mission), Major = 'M' (likely, if defective, to result in failure of an end item to perform a required mission, but not critical), Minor = no letter (significant to product quality but not likely to impair mission performance).

title: Federal Logistics Information System (FLIS) Procedures
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for Federal Logistics Information System procedures relevant to item identification and TDP logistics support data.

title: DoD Industrial Security Manual for Safeguarding Classified Information
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for requirements on safeguarding classified information that may appear within a Technical Data Package.

title: Distribution Statements on Technical Documents
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for the distribution statement markings required on technical documents, including TDP elements.

title: Withholding of Unclassified Technical Data From Public Disclosure
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for the criteria and procedures governing withholding of unclassified technical data from public disclosure.

title: Federal Standardization Manual
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B as the governing manual for federal standardization program policies and procedures.

title: Decimal Inch Drawing Sheet Size and Format
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for decimal-inch engineering drawing sheet size and format requirements.

title: Metric Drawing Sheet Size and Format
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for metric engineering drawing sheet size and format requirements.

title: Types and Applications of Engineering Drawings
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for the types and appropriate applications of engineering drawings used as TDP engineering design data.

title: Associated Lists
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for the format of associated lists (e.g. parts lists) accompanying engineering design data.

title: Revision of Engineering Drawings and Associated Documents
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for the practices governing revision of engineering drawings and associated documents.

title: Digital Product Definition Data Practices
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for digital product definition (Model Based Definition) data practices used in 3D Technical Data Packages.

title: Dimensioning and Tolerancing
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) practices used in engineering design data.

title: Engineering Drawing Practices
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B as the general engineering drawing practices standard underlying Type 2D Technical Data Packages.

title: System and Software Engineering — Software Lifecycle Processes
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B for software lifecycle process terminology (e.g. "software life cycle data"), relevant to computer software documentation TDP elements.

title: Document Management — Portable Document Format
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B as the PDF standard underlying 3Di (3-Dimensional Intelligent) viewable technical data.

title: Standard for the Exchange of Product Model Data (STEP)
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B as the standard (STEP) for neutral CAD data formats derived from 3D native models.

title: Technical Data Package: Composition, Communication, and Application
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-31000B as the National Aerospace Standard counterpart addressing Technical Data Package composition, communication, and application.

title: Drawings, Engineering and Associated Lists
summary: Referenced by DOD-STD-2101(OS) as the specification governing engineering drawings and associated lists, relevant to where characteristic classification codes are annotated on drawings.

title: Specifications, Types and Forms
summary: Referenced by DOD-STD-2101(OS) as the specification defining specification types and forms (e.g. Form 1 specifications), relevant to where classification codes and inspection requirements are annotated in specifications.

title: Engineering Drawing Practices
summary: Referenced by DOD-STD-2101(OS) as the standard for engineering drawing practices — classification codes for items described by drawings are annotated directly on MIL-STD-100 format drawings, immediately beside the characteristic call-out.

title: Sampling Procedures and Tables for Inspection by Attributes
summary: Referenced by DOD-STD-2101(OS) as a standard sampling plan source (attributes sampling, e.g. AQL-based) usable for inspecting classified characteristics.

title: Quality Assurance Terms and Definitions
summary: Referenced by DOD-STD-2101(OS) as the source for general quality assurance terminology not separately defined within that standard.

title: Sampling Procedures and Tables for Inspection by Variables for Percent Defective
summary: Referenced by DOD-STD-2101(OS) as a standard sampling plan source (variables sampling for percent defective) usable for inspecting classified characteristics.

title: Single and Multi-Level Continuous Sampling Procedures and Tables for Inspection by Attributes
summary: Referenced by DOD-STD-2101(OS) as a standard sampling plan source (continuous sampling procedures) usable for inspecting classified characteristics.

title: Guide for Sampling Inspection
summary: Referenced by DOD-STD-2101(OS) as a guidance handbook for sampling inspection, supporting selection of inspection sampling plans for classified characteristics.

title: Multi-Level Continuous Sampling Procedures and Tables for Inspection by Attributes
summary: Referenced by DOD-STD-2101(OS) as a handbook of multi-level continuous sampling procedures and tables for inspection by attributes.

title: Single-Level Continuous Sampling Procedures and Tables for Inspection by Attributes
summary: Referenced by DOD-STD-2101(OS) as a handbook of single-level continuous sampling procedures and tables for inspection by attributes.

title: Abbreviations and Acronyms for Use on Drawings and Related Documents
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-963C as the governing standard for abbreviations used in Data Item Descriptions; abbreviations not covered by ASME Y14.38 default to the GPO Style Manual.

title: Letter Symbols for Units of Measurement (SI Units, Customary Inch-Pound Units)
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-963C as the governing standard for symbols used in Data Item Descriptions; symbols not covered by IEEE 260.1 default to the GPO Style Manual.

title: DoD Forms Management Program
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-963C for DoD forms management program requirements relevant to forms referenced within a DID.

title: Information Security Program
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-963C for marking and handling requirements when a DID must contain classified material; the DID title itself may never be classified, and any classified DID must be a one-time DID.

title: Standardization Directory
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-963C as the directory listing DID Approval Authorities and data standardization area designations for each Military Department/Defense Agency.

title: United States Government Printing Office Style Manual
summary: Referenced by both MIL-STD-961 and MIL-STD-963C as the fallback style guide for grammar, abbreviations, and symbols not otherwise covered by ASME Y14.38 or IEEE 260.1.

title: Guide for Identification and Development of Metric Standards
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-961 as the Defense Standardization Program Office guide for identifying and developing metric standards, relevant to designating a specification as metric, inch-pound, or not measurement sensitive.

title: Performance Specification Guide
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-961 as the Defense Standardization Program Office guide for developing performance specifications (MIL-PRF- identifiers), which state required results and verification criteria rather than design/manufacturing methods.

title: Federal Supply Classification Groups and Classes
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-961 as the Defense Logistics Information Service cataloging handbook defining Federal Supply Classification (FSC) groups and classes, used to designate the FSC on item and material program-unique specification cover pages.

title: Federal Item Name Directory
summary: Referenced by MIL-STD-961 as the Defense Logistics Information Service directory of approved item names, used for program-unique specification titles.

title: Use of the International System of Units (SI) — The Modern Metric System
summary: Jointly published by IEEE and ASTM International; referenced by MIL-STD-961 as the definition of metric units (SI) used to distinguish metric, inch-pound, and dual-dimension specifications.

title: Defense Standardization Program Policies and Procedures
summary: Referenced in MIL-STD-961's foreword as the manual governing the procedural matters of the Defense Standardization Program — document development authorization, coordination, comment resolution, indexing, distribution, application, and document maintenance.
